A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original forecasting experiments on four datasets, with aggregate results in Tables 5–8 and per-series MAE/RMSE results in Appendix A.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report revised original forecasting results for the proposed method and its comparators on the same four datasets.

M1.justification: The central weighting and uncertainty construction change from covariance matrices W to inverse covariance matrices. v2 Section 3 uses W inverse in the empirical loss and constructs bounds from bootstrapped inverse covariance estimates in Algorithm 1. This changes the proposed procedure, although the semidefinite optimization framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Australian births, Australian tourism, Walmart sales, and Swiss electricity demand with the same represented series and forecasting tasks. The introduction's reference to five datasets persists, but neither version reports a fifth dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 5–16 retain the same comparators: Base, BU, TD, GLS, and MinT. The preliminary qualitative comparison of Prophet with ARIMA and LightGBM also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported observation/forecast periods, preprocessing, Prophet defaults, MAE/RMSE metrics, 9:1 validation split, 5,000 bootstrap samples, and alpha candidate grid remain unchanged. The revised baseline scores do not establish a change to these settings.

E4.justification: Neither version adds separate ablations, sensitivity experiments, distribution-shift tests, or case studies. Appendix A remains a presentation of per-series benchmark results; revised failure explanations do not constitute additional analyses.

E5.justification: Recalculation from unchanged tourism baseline rows shows a change from population to sample across-series standard deviations. For example, the seven BU state-level MAE ratios yield SD 0.229 with divisor 7 in v1 and 0.247 with divisor 6 in v2; TD, GLS, and MinT show the same pattern (Tables 6 and 11). No repeated-run uncertainty or significance testing is added.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced across Tables 5–8 and Appendix A. Robust's tourism total MAE changes from 975.44 to 780.57, and Walmart total RMSE from 2195.19 to 2026.11. Baseline scores also change for births, Walmart, and electricity, while tourism baseline scores remain fixed. These accompany a revised method and should not be interpreted as gains from an unchanged procedure.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces v1's equality between trace variance and expected W-weighted error with an unbiased Euclidean-error formulation. v2 also adds an inverse-covariance-weighted error inequality and a claimed invariance to positive-definite weighting matrices. The uncertainty set is redefined for inverse covariance, while Proposition 1's duality and Schur-complement proof largely retains its structure.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the objective description from worst-case expected squared error to worst-case average weighted squared residuals, and the conclusion specifies inverse-covariance uncertainty. Robust reconciliation, semidefinite reformulation, and improved forecasting remain the principal claimed contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds empirical bias and finite-sample weighting to the method's motivation and explicitly attributes some underperformance to excessive conservatism. Section 4.3 removes v1's recommendation to use a large selected alpha as an advance effectiveness diagnostic, retaining a retrospective interpretation instead. The scalability limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds an experiment-code repository address, absent from v1. Software, tuning parameters, and approximate runtime disclosures remain. Conversely, v1's Section 2.2 explanation of using shrinkage to handle singular covariance estimates is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shiratori et al. (2020) and removes Schäfer and Strimmer (2005). Panagiotelis et al. (2021) is retained and receives expanded discussion of weighted-error properties. These are limited changes within the existing hierarchical-forecasting and robust-optimization positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, reorganizes sentences within dataset descriptions, and rewrites the MinT motivation and portions of the discussion. The section, subsection, and appendix organization remains intact; most exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1, Algorithm 1, and all sixteen tables are retained with essentially the same display structures. Local reflow changes table positions and reference/appendix spacing, particularly around Tables 5–9. There is no substantial graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 removes v1's incorrect covariance-weighted trace identity, more clearly distinguishes empirical fitting from expected-error claims, and adds code-access information. These improve exposition and reproducibility documentation. The gain is limited by unexplained baseline-score revisions and a retained claim that only Robust beats Base on births, now contradicted by MinT in Table 9. Lower revised scores alone do not establish a controlled performance improvement.
